response: The presence of viral co-infection in children with acute respiratory infection (ARI) is very common, but it does not seem to have a significant impact on the severity of the disease. However, bacterial superinfection can increase the severity of the disease course. On the other hand, pneumococcal vaccination has been found to play a protective role in reducing the severity of ARI in children. Therefore, while viral co-infection itself may not influence the severity of ARI, other factors such as bacterial superinfection and vaccination status can have a significant impact on the disease outcome.
